tweetHighlights.originalBody:
Much like we did with @aisdk, we're bringing a truly open-source, runtime-agnostic solution to harness durability.

We're extending the durability infra that powers @eve and Workflows to all harnesses, like Pi and OpenCode. Local, Vercel, or DIY.

Fun fact: even Claude Code and Codex can be made durable (and observable!) this way. The catch: they're not (currently) designed for embedding, which makes them less efficient, less portable, and brings an extra sandbox requirement compared to Pi or Fx.
tweetHighlights.translatedTitle: 就像我们之前对 @aisdk 所做的那样，我们正在打造一个真正开源、与运行时无关的……
tweetHighlights.translatedBody:
就像我们之前开发 @aisdk 一样，我们正在推出一个真正开源、与运行时无关的解决方案，以实现持久性。

我们将为 @eve 和 Workflows 提供支持的持久性基础架构扩展到所有框架，例如 Pi 和 OpenCode。无论是本地部署、Vercel 还是 DIY 部署，都适用。

有趣的是：即使是 Claude Code 和 Codex 也可以通过这种方式实现持久化（并且可观察！）。但缺点是：它们（目前）并非为嵌入式应用而设计，这使得它们的效率较低、可移植性较差，并且与 Pi 或 Fx 相比，需要额外的沙箱环境。

Inference time scaling ---> Subagents --> Agent Swarms

CPU Threads --> Multi-core CPUs --> Multi-Node Distributed Systems

推理时间扩展 ---> 子智能体 --> 智能体群

CPU 线程 --> 多核 CPU --> 多节点分布式系统

历史总是惊人地相似。

If you’re a product builder in the earliest stages, the biggest advantage of having your own audience isn’t even the distribution.

It’s being able to 
- Test different ideas/angles and see what resonate with people

Signals > distribution

tweetHighlights.originalTitle: Astra did the planning, Sol 6.1 did the coding.
tweetHighlights.originalBody:
Astra did the planning, Sol 6.1 did the coding.

I found that the workflow of prompting Astra to run codex cli in worktrees works FAR better than relying on subagents.

A second agent oversaw the work to keep Astra on track. Kinda like /goal, but instead of the same agent reviewing a text file, a second agent that challenges. Wrote an OC-plugin for this "smart goal" feature.
tweetHighlights.translatedBody:
Astra 负责规划，Sol 6.1 负责编码。

我发现，在工作树中提示 Astra 运行 codex cli 的工作流程远比依赖子代理要好得多。

第二个代理负责监督工作，确保 Astra 的工作按计划进行。这有点像 /goal 命令，但不是同一个代理审查文本文件，而是第二个代理提出质疑。我为这个“智能目标”功能编写了一个 OC 插件。
